about_text: A living field guide to the Wabash country around Prophetstown — the place where the Tippecanoe meets the Wabash. One map of the region's places and events, a dashboard of its natural cycles, and a record of who's been seen. Every entry lists its source; the guide is only ever as reliable as its sources.
epigraph: People have been navigating these rivers since long before you were here, and will be long after you’re gone…

moons._note: Myaamia (Miami) lunar months — myaamia kiilhswaakani — from the Myaamia Center, Miami University / Miami Tribe of Oklahoma. Chosen because the Wabash–Tippecanoe confluence is Miami (Wea / Piankeshaw) homeland; Prophetstown itself (1808–12) was Tenskwatawa's pan-tribal town. Reckoning: the June solstice must fall inside paaphsaahka niipinwiki (mid-summer moon); when 13 lunations separate two mid-summer moons, waawiita kiilhswa 'Lost Moon' is inserted after mahkwa kiilhswa. This reproduces the Center's 2024 new year (day 7 of mahkoonsa = 2024-02-17) and their 2026 lost moon; it differs from their list of past lost-moon years at one edge case (2012/13), so it is a reckoning, not the Tribe's calendar — compare to the Center's published calendar each winter. Months begin at saakiwa, when the moon's light returns (new moon).
moons.note: Myaamia Kiilhswaakani, the Miami lunar calendar, as published by the Myaamia Center (Miami Tribe of Oklahoma). Reckoned here from the summer-solstice rule the Center describes; a reckoning, not the Tribe’s own calendar — see aacimotaatiiyankwi.org for theirs.
